description: A feature flag read inside the ad service's `GetAds` handler activated a singleton `CPULoad` that spawned 4 daemon threads each running a tight `Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis())` loop; the threads pinned CPU cores and saturated container CPU and `jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio` on the `ad` service.
mechanism: The flag is read in [`AdService.java#L172`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/AdService.java#L172): on every `getAds` gRPC call, `CPULoad.getInstance().execute()` is invoked with the boolean value of the `adHighCpu` flag. When the flag is `true`, [`CPULoad.java#L46-L52`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L46) calls `spawnLoadWorkers(4)`, which launches 4 daemon threads ([`CPULoad.java#L64-L74`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L64)). Each thread runs a tight `while(shouldRun) { Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()); }` loop ([`CPULoad.java#L101-L103`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L101)), saturating CPU cores with continuous logarithm calculations. The threads persist until the flag is toggled off, at which point `stopWorkers()` sets `shouldRun=false` on each thread. Because the workers are spawned only once (guarded by the `running` flag at line 49), repeated `getAds` calls while the flag is on do not create additional threads.

variants.description: Ad container total CPU usage rate spiked from ~0.002 to ~3.9 CPU cores, reflecting the 4 CPU-bound worker threads consuming nearly 4 full cores
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~2e6. At 14:22, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to ~3.37e8 — roughly 170x the baseline — clearly marking the onset of the CPU spike.

variants.description: Ad container user-mode CPU usage rate spiked from ~0.001 to ~3.9 CPU cores, confirming the CPU saturation is entirely user-space computation (Math.log tight loops)
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~1.2e6–1.5e6. At 14:22, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to ~3.36e8 — a ~200x increase — clearly the first timestamp of the spike.

variants.description: Host-level idle CPU ratio collapsed from ~96% to ~44%, as the 4 Logarithmizer threads from the ad service consumed the majority of available CPU capacity
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident values oscillate around 0.96. At 14:22 the value is 0.962 (still in the normal range), but at 14:23 it drops sharply to 0.619 and continues collapsing to near-zero. The last timestamp with a normal pre-incident value is 14:22, making it the onset — the last point before the idle CPU ratio collapses, indicating a sudden spike in CPU utilization.

variants.description: Total span duration (ms/s) for the frontend service. The frontend calls the CPU-saturated ad service on product pages, so its spans inherit the ad service's multi-second latency, increasing aggregate duration ~10x.
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is roughly 17-27 (mean ~21-22). There's a minor bump around 14:16-14:20 that subsides back to baseline by 14:28-14:30. The sustained spike begins at 14:31 (28.1) and climbs sharply to 50+ by 14:35, never returning to baseline. This is the clear onset of the persistent spike following the incident.

variants.description: The flagd impression counter for the adHighCpu flag with variant=on increased from 3 to 5 after the flag was toggled on, recording new evaluations of the flag returning true.
variants.onset_reasoning: The metric baseline is 0 throughout the pre-incident period. At 14:22 UTC (one minute after the incident time), the value spikes to 0.00416667, which is the first non-zero value and clearly marks the onset of the feature flag being toggled on.

logs.name: ad: High CPU-Load problempattern enabled (INFO)
logs.description: At 14:21:26.532 UTC, the ad service emitted 25 INFO logs announcing that the High CPU-Load problem pattern had been enabled.
logs.cause: Smoking-gun direct evidence of the adHighCpu flag. On every getAds invocation, AdService.java:172 calls ffClient.getBooleanValue("adHighCpu", false, ctx) and passes the result to CPULoad.execute(enabled). When enabled=true, CPULoad.java:48 logs "High CPU-Load problempattern enabled" at INFO and, if not already running, spawns 4 daemon Logarithmizer threads (CPULoad.java:50, 64-73) that tight-loop Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()) to saturate CPU. Note the log is not an error — the ad service continues serving requests successfully, just under CPU pressure.
logs.source: ad service (Java, oteldemo.problempattern.CPULoad logger via OpenTelemetry Java agent)
